Build the compiled CausalStructures.jl library

Source: R/install.R
install_backend.Rd

Compiles CausalStructures.jl with your Julia (>= 1.13) into the shared library that every function of the package calls. Run it once after installing or updating CausalStructures, and again (with force = TRUE) if the Julia it was built with is removed, for example by a juliaup update.

Usage

install_backend(
  julia = NULL,
  ask = interactive(),
  force = FALSE,
  update = FALSE,
  project = NULL
)

Arguments

julia

Path to the julia binary to build with. Defaults to the JULIA environment variable, else julia on the PATH.

ask

Ask for confirmation before building? Defaults to interactive().

force

Rebuild even if a library for this version of CausalStructures already exists? Implied by update and project.

update

Use the newest dependency versions the Project.toml allows instead of those in its Manifest.toml?

project

Path to a directory with the Project.toml (and optionally a Manifest.toml) to build from, instead of the shipped ones.

Value

The path to the library, invisibly.

Details

Julia downloads CausalStructures.jl and its dependencies into its package depot (~/.julia unless JULIA_DEPOT_PATH says otherwise) and compiles them, which takes several minutes. The library is written to a directory per package version under tools::R_user_dir("CausalStructures", "data"), and libraries built for other versions are removed from there.

By default the dependencies are the exact versions in the Manifest.toml shipped with this version of CausalStructures, which are the versions it was tested with. update = TRUE instead uses the newest versions the shipped Project.toml allows, e.g. to get a CausalStructures.jl bug fix before the next release of this package. project builds from your own Julia environment: start from a copy of system.file("julia", "Project.toml", package = "CausalStructures"), keep its name, UUID and dependencies, and change e.g. the [compat] bounds, or add a [sources] section to use a development version of CausalStructures.jl.

Julia can only be started once per R process, so a library that replaces one already loaded is used from the next R session on.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
install_backend()

# The newest CausalStructures.jl release, instead of the tested one
install_backend(update = TRUE)
} # }
